method: Each entry RFC and every RFC the task depends on (found through links in the text: absolute github.com URLs, rust-lang.github.io/rfcs URLs or RFC NNNN references) was read in full, and a section was kept only if its own text, from its heading to the next real heading of any level (lines starting with # inside code fences do not count), states a fact the task cannot be done correctly without; when a fact is repeated, the most specific section that states it was kept.

tasks.task: Write the Rust 2024 edition migration lint for return position impl Trait from RFC 3617: wherever the 2024 lifetime capture rules would make an opaque type capture lifetime parameters that it does not capture in Rust 2021, suggest a use<..> bound that keeps the 2021 set of captured parameters. Add UI tests for a free function with a named and an elided lifetime, an inherent method of a type with a lifetime parameter, a method in a trait impl, a function with an argument position impl Trait, and a nested impl Trait under a for<'a> binder.

required.heading: Lifetime Capture Rules 2024
required.why: Rust 2021 rule (all type parameters, lifetimes only when named in the bounds) for RPIT on free and inherent functions, the 2024 change, and that RPITIT and ATPIT capture everything in all editions

required.heading: Syntax
required.why: grammar of the suggestion: use<..> right after impl and before the bounds, lifetimes and identifiers only, may be empty

required.heading: Avoiding capture of higher ranked lifetimes in nested opaques
required.why: in 2024 a nested opaque under for<..> captures the higher ranked lifetime and fails to compile; use<> avoids it

required.heading: Migration strategy for Lifetime Capture Rules 2024
required.why: the lint inserts use<..> to keep the captured set and turns argument position impl Trait into named type parameters

required.heading: Stabilization strategy
required.why: use<..> must list every in-scope type and const parameter; both were already captured in 2021

required.heading: Capturing lifetimes from an inherent method signature
required.why: in 2024 the elided lifetime of &self is captured together with the named and outer parameters

required.heading: Return position `impl Trait` in Trait (RPITIT)
required.why: RPIT in a trait impl captures all outer impl and signature parameters in all editions, so those methods need no migration

critical.constraint: RPIT in a trait impl and RPITIT in a trait already capture every in-scope parameter in all editions, so the lint must not fire on them; only RPIT on free functions and inherent associated functions and methods changes
critical.heading: Return position `impl Trait` in Trait (RPITIT)

critical.constraint: The suggested use<..> keeps exactly the set captured in Rust 2021, and an argument position impl Trait must first become a named type parameter because use<..> can only list named parameters
critical.heading: Migration strategy for Lifetime Capture Rules 2024

critical.constraint: use<..> must list every in-scope type and const parameter; only lifetimes may be left out
critical.heading: Stabilization strategy

critical.constraint: A nested impl Trait under a for<'a> binder fails in Rust 2024 because it captures the higher ranked lifetime; the fix is use<> or a list without that lifetime
critical.heading: Avoiding capture of higher ranked lifetimes in nested opaques

tasks.task: For RFC 3875, make Cargo work out the standard library dependencies of each package for the current target and pass them to rustc: the implicit ones when the package declares none, otherwise the explicit builtin ones from every dependency table that applies to the target, each with the right --extern modifiers and public or private status. Add tests for a target whose default is only core, a target-specific alloc dependency, an optional std behind a feature, and a std dependency declared only in dev-dependencies.

required.heading: Proposal
required.why: builtin source rules, the implicit set and what turns it off, noprelude only for implicit dependencies, the test crate, optional dependency checks, -Zcrate-attr=no_std, target-specific tables

required.heading: Public and private dependencies
required.why: implicit dependencies are public, explicit ones private by default

required.heading: `dev-dependencies` and `build-dependencies`
required.why: a builtin entry in dev-dependencies also turns off the implicit set; build-dependencies cannot have builtin entries and build scripts and proc macros use the pre-built std

required.heading: Standard library crate stability
required.why: the target's default set comes from standard_library_support.default, read with rustc --print target-standard-library-support

required.heading: Why use `nounused` with `--extern`?
required.why: every standard library crate passed with --extern also gets the nounused modifier so unused_crate_dependencies does not fire

critical.constraint: Any explicit standard library dependency, builtin or path, in a dependency table that applies to the current target turns off all implicit standard library dependencies
critical.heading: Proposal

critical.constraint: Explicit builtin dependencies are passed without noprelude and implicit ones with it; this overrides the RFC 3874 rule that every standard library crate gets noprelude
critical.heading: Proposal

critical.constraint: core can never be optional, an optional std needs a non-optional core or alloc, and when std is optional or missing Cargo passes -Zcrate-attr=no_std
critical.heading: Proposal

critical.constraint: The implicit set is the target's standard_library_support.default (core only for armv7a-none-eabi, std for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu); the JSON example that prints default core for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu is wrong
critical.heading: Standard library crate stability

tasks.task: Implement default field values from RFC 3681 in rustc: accept field: Type = expr on named fields of structs and enum variants, type-check struct expressions that end in .. without a base, and make #[derive(Default)] on a struct use the field defaults. Add UI tests for a default whose value panics, a struct with private defaulted fields built from another module, a #[non_exhaustive] struct with a defaulted field, and a struct without defaults written as S { .. }.

required.heading: `#[non_exhaustive]` interactions
required.why: default field values are allowed only on types without #[non_exhaustive]

required.heading: Defaults for `enum`s
required.why: variant fields can have defaults; #[non_exhaustive] on the enum has no effect on them, on a variant it acts as on a struct

required.heading: Grammar
required.why: the = expr field syntax and the two new struct expression forms that end in .. without a base

required.heading: Defining defaults
required.why: a default must be a constant expression that coerces to the field type, may use generic parameters, and is evaluated only at instantiation

required.heading: `#[derive(Default)]`
required.why: the derived default() leaves out defaulted fields and uses Default::default() for the others

required.heading: Privacy: building `struct`s with private defaulted fields
required.why: visibility rules do not change: every defaulted field must be visible where S { .. } is written

required.heading: "Empty" types and types without default field values
required.why: .. without a base is allowed only when the type has at least one defaulted field

critical.constraint: A default must be a constant expression that coerces to the field type, and it is evaluated only when a struct expression uses it, so field: usize = panic!() compiles as long as each use gives that field
critical.heading: Defining defaults

critical.constraint: S { .. } is rejected where a defaulted field is not visible; the Java prior-art remark that the RFC permits defaults for private fields is wrong
critical.heading: Privacy: building `struct`s with private defaulted fields

critical.constraint: Default field values are not allowed on #[non_exhaustive] types; the unresolved question's idea of accepting Config { width: 640, height: 480, .. } is not adopted
critical.heading: `#[non_exhaustive]` interactions

critical.constraint: .. without a base needs at least one defaulted field, so S { .. } on a struct without defaults is an error
critical.heading: "Empty" types and types without default field values
